data.title: Review a route with dimensional proxies
data.summary: A room, user-supplied route requirements and a turning-envelope proxy. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: Godot documents 3D scene formats, export conventions and import configuration.

prerequisites: An authorized Blender / Three.js environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: A room, user-supplied route requirements and a turning-envelope proxy.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent accessibility route workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: A room, user-supplied route requirements and a turning-envelope proxy. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Inspect the supplied requirements and model their dimensions explicitly
Move the route/turning proxy through entrances and around furniture
Record clearances and conflicts at named checkpoints with screenshots or measurements

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned review a route with dimensional proxies candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: Every checkpoint retains its measured clearance and requirement source
Conflicts remain open until a qualified reviewer resolves them
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: The workflow assists review and does not certify legal accessibility compliance.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.
Cloud chat cannot directly control a local 3D app without an appropriate authorized bridge. Tool access, model availability, paid services and rendering resources must be checked separately.
tips: Keep jurisdiction-specific requirements separate from the geometry model.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me review a route with dimensional proxies in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: A room, user-supplied route requirements and a turning-envelope proxy. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: Every checkpoint retains its measured clearance and requirement source; Conflicts remain open until a qualified reviewer resolves them. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.
